stem: A nursing unit is considering staff self-scheduling. Which statement best reflects the evidence?

options.A: Self-scheduling can improve staff control, scheduling satisfaction, and work-life balance, but outcomes depend on implementation, fairness, and unit coverage requirements.
options.B: Self-scheduling eliminates the need for staffing rules, coverage standards, and manager oversight.
options.C: Self-scheduling consistently worsens autonomy and job satisfaction in every nursing setting.
options.D: Self-scheduling requires each nurse to choose shifts independently without coordination with unit needs.

rationale: Systematic reviews of healthcare self-rostering report benefits such as greater control or empowerment, scheduling/job satisfaction, and work-life balance, but also identify inconsistent results and implementation challenges including fairness, coverage, and sustainability. Self-scheduling therefore requires structured rules and coordination rather than unrestricted individual choice. A is correct.
educational_objective: Describe both the potential workforce benefits and implementation constraints of nurse self-scheduling.
source_document_title: The impact of electronic and self-rostering systems on healthcare organisations and healthcare workers: A mixed-method systematic review
source_locator: Results and Conclusion — benefits, equity/implementation limitations, and organizational outcomes
source_claim_supported: Self-rostering can improve staff satisfaction, control/empowerment and work-life balance, but outcomes and equity depend on implementation and organizational context.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — staffing, scheduling, and resource management

source_original.stem: A nursing unit implements a self-scheduling model, in which staff have significant input into creating their own work schedules within defined parameters, and a skeptical manager on another unit predicts this will just create chaos with no real benefit. This model is generally instead associated with:

options.A: Self-scheduling can improve autonomy and satisfaction when coverage and fairness rules are clear
options.B: Self-scheduling removes the need for staffing rules, coverage standards, or manager oversight
options.C: Self-scheduling consistently decreases staff autonomy and work-life control after adoption
options.D: Self-scheduling requires every nurse to choose shifts independently without team coordination

source_original.rationale: Self-scheduling models, which give staff meaningful input into their own schedules within defined parameters (ensuring adequate unit coverage and fairness), are generally associated with improved staff satisfaction and a sense of autonomy and control over their work-life balance, when implemented thoughtfully with clear guidelines.
source_original.source_detail: Workforce scheduling/engagement resources support staff participation and structured coverage requirements; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the vague AONL resource-page citation with a PubMed-indexed 2024 systematic review and corrected the original overly positive framing by explicitly incorporating inconsistent outcomes, fairness, coverage, and implementation context; difficulty reduced to medium.

audit_findings.currentness: Review checked 2026-08-17; a 2026 observational study is directionally supportive but was not needed for the final claim.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final answer reflects both reported benefits and documented implementation/equity limitations.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is uniquely consistent with the systematic review.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed skeptical-manager narrative and balanced the keyed answer with limitations.
audit_findings.blueprint: Staff scheduling fits Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the systematic review's results/conclusion and confirmed the evidence is not uniformly positive; A remains uniquely defensible.
